title: Cross-Lingual Response Consistency in Large Language Models: An ILR-Informed Evaluation of Claude Across Six Languages

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating response consistency across six languages (English, French, Romanian, Spanish, Italian, German) using 12 semantically equivalent prompt clusters. The study compares automated quantitative metrics (response length, list usage, surface similarity to an English baseline) and qualitative expert assessment based on the Interagency Language Roundtable (ILR) framework to identify performance and pragmatic disparities between languages.

Qualitatively assessing model outputs generated in different languages to detect the imposition of English-centric discourse norms and the absence of culture-specific content (e.g., local mourning traditions or institutional resources). The methodology involves expert evaluation of responses for cultural calibration, identifying whether the model generates natively grounded cultural references or defaults to culturally neutralized English-language templates.
